Rashi on Zevachim 14a:10:1.hebrew: אי מחוץ לזמנו - נילף במה מצינו:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:10:1.english: If [we derive it] from [intent to eat it] beyond its time - [we may respond:] From what [other case] do we find [this]?

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:11:1.english: If from not for its sake - and by a kal vachomer, as above.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:11:2.hebrew: שכן נוהג בבמה - [בקרבן במת יחיד בשעת היתר הבמות, שהרי שנוי קדש הוא. תאמר בחוץ למקומו, דלא שאין מחיצה בבמה] וכל הבקעה מקומו עד סוף העולם:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:11:2.english: For it applies to a private altar - [That is, in the offering of a private altar at the time when private altars were permitted, for it is a change of sacred status. Could you say this of [intent to eat] outside its place? No, for there is no partition at a private altar,] and the whole plain is its place, to the end of the world.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:12:1.hebrew: ומשני שלא לשמו במאי נוהג - באיזה קרבן אתה מוצא פסולו? בפסח וחטאת. והני בבמה לא קרבי, דתנן לקמן (זבחים דף קיז.): כל הנידר ונידב קרב בבמה, ושאינו נידר ונידב אינו קרב בבמה:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:12:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Not for its sake — in what does it apply? - In which offering do you find its disqualification? In a Paschal offering and a sin offering. And these are not sacrificed on a private altar, as we learned later (Zevachim 117a): Anything that is vowed or brought as a voluntary offering is sacrificed on a private altar, but whatever is not vowed or voluntary is not sacrificed on a private altar:

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:13:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - חוץ למקומו מחוץ לזמנו אתי, ולא פרכינן שכן כרת, דהיקשא הוא דאיתקש חוץ למקומו לחוץ לזמנו בפ' שני (לקמן זבחים דף כח.) בקרא אחרינא, דאמרינן "אם האכל יאכל ביום השלישי" - זה מחשבת חוץ לזמנו, "לא יחשב לו פיגול יהיה" - קרא יתירא הוא, לאתויי חוץ למקומו. וכיון דאיתקוש, גמרינן מהדדי, ואין משיבין על ההיקש:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:13:1.english: And if you wish, say - [The law of] outside its place is derived from [the law of] outside its time, and we do not refute [this derivation by arguing] "for [outside its time] involves karet," because it is by juxtaposition that outside its place is juxtaposed to outside its time, in the second chapter (below, Zevachim 28a), in another verse, as we say: "If any of the flesh ... is at all eaten on the third day" - this is the thought of outside its time; "it shall not be imputed to the one who offers it; it shall be an abhorred thing [piggul]" - this is a superfluous verse, to bring in [the case of] outside its place. And since they are juxtaposed, we derive them from one another, and one does not refute a juxtaposition.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:1.hebrew: אמר רבא את"ל ר' שמעון סבר לה כבריה דאמר - לקמן בפ' שני (זבחים דף כ.):
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:1.english: Rava said: If you say that Rabbi Shimon holds like his son, who said - Later, in the second chapter (Zevachim 20a).

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:2.hebrew: בין האולם למזבח צפון - חלק צפוני שבעזרה שבין האולם ולמזבח, אע"ג דלא קרינן ביה "על ירך המזבח צפונה", דהא במערבו של מזבח הוא, הוי צפון לענין שחיטת קדשי קדשים:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:2.english: Between the Entrance Hall and the altar is north - The northern part of the courtyard that is between the Entrance Hall and the altar, even though we cannot apply to it "on the side of the altar northward" (Leviticus 1:11), since it is to the west of the altar, is considered north with regard to the slaughtering of the most sacred offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:3.hebrew: אין מחשבה מועלת בחטאות הפנימיות - אפילו לפסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:3.english: Intent is not effective for the inner sin offerings - even to disqualify [them].

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:4.hebrew: אלא מפתח האולם ולפנים - שאם חישב בהולכת הדם ממקום שחיטתו עד האולם, אינה מחשבה, שהרי אפשר לבטל הולכה זו, לשחוט אצל פתח האולם. אבל אי סבר כרבי יוסי, דפליג אדרבי אלעזר בר' שמעון ואומר אין צפון אלא כנגד המזבח, מקיר המזבח צפוני עד כותל העזרה צפונית — הויא לה עבודה שאין יכול לבטלה, דהא חטאת טעונה צפון לשחיטתה, דכתיב (ויקרא ד, כד) במקום אשר תשחט העולה וגו', וצפון בעולה כתיב:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:14:4.english: Only from the doorway of the Entrance Hall inward - For if he had a prohibited thought while conveying the blood from the place of its slaughter to the Entrance Hall, it is not a [disqualifying] thought, since it is possible to eliminate this conveying by slaughtering next to the doorway of the Entrance Hall. But if he holds like Rabbi Yosei, who disagrees with Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, and says that "north" is only opposite the altar, from the northern wall of the altar to the northern wall of the courtyard — then it is a service that he cannot eliminate, for a sin offering requires the north for its slaughter, as it is written, "In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered" (Leviticus 4:24), etc., and "north" is written regarding the burnt offering:

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:15:1.hebrew: ואת"ל - ר' שמעון סבר לה כר' יהודה דאמר לקמן בפ' קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף נט.) תוך עזרה מקדש, כלומר כל רצפת העזרה בין האולם ולמזבח מקודשת להקטיר חלבים כמזבח עצמו, דכתיב (מלכים א ח) ״ביום ההוא קדש המלך את תוך החצר״. ותניא לקמן ״דברים ככתבן״, דברי ר' יהודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:15:1.english: And if you say - Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who says below, in the chapter [beginning] Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 59a), that the interior of the courtyard sanctifies, i.e., the entire floor of the courtyard between the Entrance Hall and the altar is sanctified for burning fats, like the altar itself, as it is written: "On that day the king sanctified the middle of the court." And it is taught below: "[Verses are to be understood] as they are written" — [these are] the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:15:2.hebrew: אין מחשבה מועלת - לר' שמעון בהולכת בזיכי לחם הפנים, שהן מתירין את הלחם כדם המתיר את הבשר וכקומץ המתיר את השיריים, והלחם מתפגל במחשבת עבודת הבזיכים הואיל והן מתירין. רבי שמעון אי כרבי יהודה סבר לה, אין מחשבת הולכה מועלת בה לפסול אלא מפתח היכל ולחוץ — משהגיע לפתח היכל עד שמגיע ליציאת אולם לרצפת העזרה שלפניו. דבכל ההיכל לא מהניא מחשבה, שהרי כל ההיכל כשר להושיב שם שלחן לסדר עליו עד הפתח, ואולם כי עזרה סבירא לן, ומן האולם ולחוץ נמי לא מהניא מחשבה בהולכה, שהרי אפשר להקטירו על רצפת העזרה מיד אם ירצה, נמצאת הולכתו עד המזבח שלא לצורך:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:15:2.english: Intent is not effective - According to Rabbi Shimon, [intent] in conveying the bowls of the showbread, since they permit the bread, like the blood that permits the meat and like the handful that permits the remainder, and the bread becomes piggul through intent during the service of the bowls, since they permit [it]. Rabbi Shimon, if he holds like Rabbi Yehuda, [holds that] intent of conveying is not effective in it to disqualify, except from the entrance of the Sanctuary outward — from when it reaches the entrance of the Sanctuary until it reaches the exit of the Entrance Hall to the floor of the Temple courtyard before it. For within the whole Sanctuary intent is not effective, since the entire Sanctuary is fit to place the table there and to arrange [the bread] upon it, up to the entrance. But the Entrance Hall, we hold, is like the courtyard, and from the Entrance Hall outward too, intent in conveying is not effective, since it is possible to burn it immediately on the floor of the courtyard if one wishes, so its conveyance to the altar turns out to be unnecessary.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:16:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואת"ל סבר רבי שמעון קדושת אולם והיכל חדא היא אין מחשבה מועלת אלא מפתח אולם ולחוץ - כלומר ה' אמות של עובי כותל פתחו של אולם. דבכל חללו של אולם לא מהניא, דכפנים דמי; וחוץ לפתח לא מהניא, דאפשר להקטיר שם:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:16:1.english: This is the correct text: And if you say that Rabbi Shimon holds that the sanctity of the Entrance Hall and the Sanctuary is one, prohibited intent is effective only from the doorway of the Entrance Hall outward - That is, the five cubits of the thickness of the wall of the doorway of the Entrance Hall. For in the entire interior space of the Entrance Hall it is not effective, since it is like the inside [of the Sanctuary]; and outside the doorway it is not effective, since it is possible to burn [the incense] there.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:17:1.hebrew: ואת"ל סבר לה תוך פתח האולם כלפנים אין מחשבה מועלת אפילו פסיעה שלימה אלא בכדי הושטת ידו - עומד בפתח האולם ומושיט ידו לרצפה, היינו הולכה ומהניא בה מחשבה:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:17:1.english: And if you say that he holds that inside the doorway of the Entrance Hall is like inside, intent is not effective [for conveying] even a full step, but only [for] the time it takes to stretch out his hand - [If the priest] stands in the doorway of the Entrance Hall and stretches out his hand to the floor [of the courtyard], this is [considered] conveying, and intent is effective for it.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:18:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ואם תמצי לומר הולכה שלא ברגל לא שמה הולכה אין מחשבה מועלת כלל - דהא הושטת ידו הולכה שלא ברגל היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:18:1.english: So we read: "And if you say that conveying not by foot is not considered conveying, intent is not effective at all" - For extending one's hand is conveying not by foot.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:1:1.hebrew: כל קרבן שאינו על מזבח החיצון כשלמים - כך נלמד שלמדנו מהם פיגול לכל הזבחים, ולכן אין בו משום פיגול, לקמן בפרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף מג.):
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:1:1.english: Any offering that is not [offered] on the external altar like peace offerings - This is derived because we learned from them [the law of] piggul for all sacrifices, and therefore it is not subject to piggul. [This is discussed] below in the chapter of Beit Shammai (Zevachim 43a).

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:20:1.hebrew: ויזרקו הכהנים את הדם מידם - "מידם" של שוחטין משמע, ושוחטין זרים נינהו, ואשמועינן קרא שהזרים לוקחין אותו מיד המקבל ומוליכין אותו לזרוק:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:20:1.english: “And the priests sprinkled the blood from their hand” - “From their hand” implies [from the hand] of the slaughterers, and the slaughterers are non-priests. And the verse teaches us that non-priests take it from the hand of the one who received [it] and convey it to be sprinkled.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:2:1.hebrew: בחטאות החיצונות - אינה מפגלת, דלא כתיב בהו "וטבל", אלא "ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת באצבעו", וההיא לקיחה קבלה היא, ומינה ילפינן קבלה לקמן באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מח.):
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:2:1.english: In the external sin offerings - [Dipping the finger] does not render [the offering] piggul, for it is not written regarding them "and he shall dip," but rather "and the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger." And that "taking" is [the equivalent of] receiving [the blood], and from it we derive [the law of] receiving, later in [the chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 48a).

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:4:1.hebrew: איצטריכא, מהו דתימא הואיל וכתיב ולקח - דמשמע הוא בעצמו יקח:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:4:1.english: It was necessary; lest you say, since it is written, “And he shall take” - For this implies that he himself must take.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:4:2.hebrew: ואי אתי קוף ורמי להו אידיה - על אצבעו, בעי מיהדר ומשקל. אלמא, ולקח נמי אאצבעו קאי, שיטבול אצבעו. אימא כמאן דכתיב וטבל דמי:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:4:2.english: And if a monkey comes and places it on his hand - on his finger, he must go back and take [blood again]. Evidently, "and he shall take" also refers to his finger, that he dips his finger. Say that it is as if "and he shall dip" is written:

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:5:1.hebrew: להכי לא כתביה טבילה - בהדיא, אלא כתב קבלה. ומדסמכיה אאצבעו ונתן, הוא דיליף לטבול אצבעו, שצריך ליקח בעצמו ולטבול. דמשמע הכי, דלא תהא טבילת אצבע עבודה חשובה בהן לפגל, מדלא אחשבה קרא להצריכה בפירוש. ומשמע הכי, שצריכה היא לטבול כחטאות החיצונה, ולא דלישקל קוף ולירמייה לדם על האצבע, דבעינן לקיחת אצבע מעליותא, דולקח נמי אאצבע קאי:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:5:1.english: For this reason Scripture did not write dipping - explicitly; rather, it wrote receiving. And from the fact that it connected it to "with his finger" and "and he shall place," he derives [the law] to dip his finger, that he must take [the blood] himself and dip. For it indicates this: that the dipping of the finger should not be an essential service in these [sin offerings] such that it could render the offering piggul, since Scripture did not deem it important enough to require it explicitly. And it indicates that: that he does need to dip, like the external sin offerings, and not that a monkey should take and throw the blood onto the finger, for we require a proper taking by the finger, as "and he shall take" also refers to the finger:

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:6:1.hebrew: שאי אפשר לבטלה - דלאו אורח ארעא לשחוט בהיכל, ועל כרחו הוא שוחטו בעזרה ומוליכה בהיכל לקרנות מזבח פנימי ולהזאת פרוכת:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:6:1.english: That it is impossible to nullify it - For it is not the way to slaughter inside the Sanctuary, and necessarily one slaughters it in the Courtyard and conveys [the blood] into the Sanctuary, to the horns of the inner altar and for the sprinkling toward the curtain.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:7:1.hebrew: כל שאינו - כל קרבן שאין מתן דמו על מזבח החיצון, לאפוקי חטאות הפנימיות. וקס"ד דה"ה לפסול דשלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:7:1.english: Any [offering] that is not - Any offering whose blood-application is not on the external altar, excluding the inner sin offerings. And the initial thought (the Gemara's assumption) is that the same applies to the disqualification of [an offering slaughtered] not for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:8:1.hebrew: מודה הוא לפסול - נהי דאין בהן פיגול להתחייב כרת על אכילתו, אבל מודה הוא דמחשבה חוץ לזמנו פוסלתו מק"ו. והכי נמי הוה מצי לתרוצי ליה: אנן במחשבה שלא לשמו קיימינא דפסלה בהו, אלא דבעי רבי יוסי בר' חנינא לאשמועינן דמחשבת חוץ לזמנו פסלה בהו לר"ש:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:8:1.english: He concedes to disqualify - Granted that there is no piggul in them, such that one would incur karet for eating it, nevertheless he concedes that intent [to eat it] beyond its time disqualifies it, by an a fortiori inference. And likewise [the Gemara] could have answered him: We are dealing with intent [to offer it] not for its own sake, which disqualifies them. But Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Ḥanina wanted to teach us that, according to Rabbi Shimon, intent beyond its time [also] disqualifies them.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:8:2.hebrew: חוץ לזמנו הפוסל בשלמים כו' - ומיהו, כרת לא נפקא לן בו מינה, דהא ק"ו מכח שלא לשמו אתי, ודיו להבא מן הדין להיות כנדון:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:8:2.english: [Intent to eat] beyond its time, which disqualifies peace offerings, etc. - However, we do not derive karet from it, for this a fortiori argument comes from the case of [sacrifice] not for its own sake, and it suffices for the conclusion derived by the argument to be like the case from which it is derived.

Rashi on Zevachim 14a:9:1.hebrew: חוץ למקומו מנא לן - דהא חוץ למקומו נמי בשלמים כתיב, ומינייהו גמרינן לכל הזבחים. ולר' שמעון, דלא גמר מינייהו אלא חיצונות כמותן, מנ"ל דפסלה בפנימיות:
Rashi on Zevachim 14a:9:1.english: Outside its area — from where do we derive [this]? - For [the law of] outside its area is also written regarding peace offerings, and from them we derive [the law] for all sacrifices. But according to Rabbi Shimon, who derives from them only that outer [offerings] are like them, from where do we know that it disqualifies [the offering] in the case of inner [offerings]?

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 14a:19.english: If a person disqualified from the priesthood conveyed the blood, whether at the beginning (where a priest conveyed it afterward) or at the end (where a priest conveyed it at the beginning), the offering is disqualified. This is in accordance with the conclusion of the sugya (Rambam, Sefer Avoda, Hilkhot Pesulei HaMukdashin 1:27).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Zevachim 14a:19.english: The Amora (in this restricted sense) is identical to the Meturgeman in Mishnaic language. The Meturgeman in the Sages’ lectures was usually a Sage (and sometimes even an important Sage) whose role was to translate the Sage’s words from Hebrew to Aramaic, and also to say them loudly (so sometimes there was more than one Meturgeman, if they needed to make it heard to many). Often, the Meturgeman would not only translate but also explain, for the Sage would state the main ideas, while the Meturgeman would elaborate and develop them. And for this reason, the Sages of the Talmud called themselves Amoraim, as they saw their role as a kind of interpreters in this sense for the Sages of the Mishna.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 14a:19.english: Abaye said to Rav Ḥisda’s interpreter: He asked Rav Ḥisda: What is the halakha with regard to a non-priest (one who is not a priest) conveying the blood? Is it disqualified, like other rites?

Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:15:1.hebrew: הג"ה תוך עזרה מקדש - טעמא דרבי יהודה לקמן בפרק קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף נט.). וצריך לדקדק לר' יהודה, כיון דעזרה מקדש היכי משכחת לה בפסולין, דאם ירדו לא יעלו? וי"ל דמשכחת לה [באותם] דירדו בלשכה או באולם או על גבי דף, ועדיף מאויר דאמר פ"ב (לקמן זבחים כו.): תלה ושחט פסול. א"נ שחט על הרצפה ואח"כ נתן על הדף, דהשתא ירדו. וצ"ע, דלקמן (זבחים דף קכ.) מבעיא להו: ירדו מהו שיעלו? [וי"ל דשחט על הרצפה [ואח"כ נתן על הדף]. ועוד יש לומר דמודה רבי יהודה בדמים לקמן דבעי מזבח, והדם לא עלה ברצפה. ותו, דלשון אם עלו דנקט היינו לדינא דקודם דאתא דוד וקדיש רצפה, וקודם בנין שלמה. הג"ה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:15:1.english: Haggah (gloss): "The interior of the Temple courtyard sanctifies" - The reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda is [given] below in the chapter Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 59a). And one must examine, according to Rabbi Yehuda: Since the courtyard sanctifies, how would one find [a case] among disqualified offerings, [given the rule] that if they descended [from the altar] they are not to go up again? And one can say that it is found [in the case of] those that descended in the chamber, or in the Entrance Hall, or on top of a board, which is better than [mere] air, as [the Mishnah] says in chapter 2 (below, Zevachim 26a): If one hung [the animal] and slaughtered it, it is disqualified. Alternatively, [if] one slaughtered on the floor and afterward placed [the offering] on the board, for now they have descended. But this requires further study, for below (Zevachim 120a) they raise the question: If they descended, may they go up? [And one can say that he slaughtered on the floor [and afterward placed it on the board]. And furthermore, one can say that Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding blood, below, that it requires an altar, and the blood did not go up on the floor. And also, the expression "if they went up" that [the Mishnah] used refers to the law of before David came and sanctified the floor, and before the building of Solomon. End of gloss:

Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:8:1.hebrew: מודה היה לפסול מקל וחומר - מכאן מתרצים ההיא דפ' הנזקין (גיטין דף נד: ושם), דקאמר ר' יוסי: כהן גדול ביום הכפורים יוכיח, דכי אמר פיגול מהימן. ור' יוסי סבירא ליה כר"ש בפ' הקומץ זוטא (מנחות דף יד.), דאין פיגול אלא בדבר הנעשה על מזבח החיצון. ולמאי דאמר הכא דמודה הוא לפסול — ניחא, דפיגול לאו דוקא. ועוד יש לפרש היינו שלא לשמה, ולא נהירא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:8:1.english: He concedes that it is disqualified by an a fortiori argument - From here they resolve that [passage] in the chapter Hanizakin (Gittin 54b, there), where Rabbi Yose says: The High Priest on Yom Kippur proves [the point], for when he says [that the offering is] piggul, he is trusted. And Rabbi Yose holds like Rabbi Shimon in the chapter Hakometz Zuta (Menachot 14a), that there is no piggul except in something done on the outer altar. But according to what [the Gemara] says here, that he concedes that it is disqualified, it works out well, for [the word] piggul [there] is not meant precisely. And one could further explain that it refers to [intent] not for its own sake, but this is not clear.

Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:8:2.hebrew: ומה שלא לשמן כו' - תימה: מה לשלא לשמן, שכן נוהג בד' עבודות; תאמר בחוץ לזמנו, שאינו נוהג אלא בזריקה? וכי האי גוונא פריך לעיל (זבחים דף ד.): (מה לחוץ לזמנו, שכן כרת). ויש לומר דאי הוה פריך הכי, הוה עביד ק"ו משנוי בעלים, דהוי כפיגל בזריקה. ומיהו קשה: מה לשנוי בעלים, שכן פוסל בזביחה בפסח או בזריקה לחודיה? וי"ל דשלא לשמן יוכיח, וילפינן במה הצד משנוי קדש ושנוי בעלים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 14a:8:2.english: "Just as [sacrifice] not for its sake..." etc. - This is puzzling: What [argument is there] from [intent] not for its sake, since it applies to four services? Would you say the same of [intent beyond its time], which applies only to the sprinkling? And is this the kind of argument [the Gemara] refutes earlier (Zevachim 4a): ("What [argument is there] from [intent] beyond its time, since it carries [the penalty of] karet?") And one can answer that had [the Gemara] refuted in this way, [Rabbi Yosei] would have made an a fortiori argument from a change of owner, which is like [intent that makes it] piggul with regard to the sprinkling. Yet this is difficult: What [argument is there] from a change of owner, since it disqualifies at the slaughter in the case of the Pesach offering, or at the sprinkling alone? And one can say that [intent] not for its sake will prove [the point], and we derive it through the "what is common to them" argument from a change of sanctity and a change of owner:

Zevachim 14a:19.english: Abaye said to Rav Ḥisda’s interpreter: Ask Rav Ḥisda: What is the halakha with regard to a non-priest conveying the blood? Is the offering disqualified, like other sacrificial rites?

Zevachim 14a:6.english: Rabbi Shimon deems the offering fit if the prohibited intent was during the rite of conveying the blood to the altar. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Rabbi Shimon concedes that prohibited intent during the conveying of the blood of inner sin offerings disqualifies them, since with regard to those offerings, it is an indispensable rite. Because the blood must be sprinkled inside the Sanctuary and an inner sin offering cannot be slaughtered inside the Sanctuary, conveying the blood into the Sanctuary is always necessary for such offerings.
